description: Class taxonomy used for per-class scores, plus the scales the hardening planner and the scoring model use. Every class rolls up into exactly one of the four CHIMERA detection categories.

categories.environment_artifact: Hardware, firmware, driver and OS artifacts that a virtual or emulated machine leaves behind.
categories.timing: Clock, cycle-counter and scheduling discrepancies caused by virtualisation, emulation or instrumentation.
categories.behavioural_interaction: Absence of a real person: no input, no wear-and-tear, no history.
categories.design_specific: Quirks of a particular analysis platform: its tools, accounts, network, instrumentation and configuration.

cpu.title: CPU and instruction set
cpu.summary: CPUID leaves, brand strings, descriptor tables, privileged and undefined instruction behaviour.

firmware.title: Firmware (SMBIOS / ACPI / BIOS)
firmware.summary: Vendor strings, serials, UUIDs and table layout in SMBIOS, ACPI and BIOS data.

hardware.title: Devices and peripherals
hardware.summary: PCI/USB/PnP devices, disks, GPU, NIC, audio, monitors, sensors, battery, thermal and fans.

resources.title: Resource sizing
resources.summary: Core count, RAM, disk size, screen resolution: values sandboxes provision too small.

guest_tools.title: Guest tools, drivers and services
guest_tools.summary: Hypervisor guest additions, paravirtual drivers, kernel modules and their services.

artifacts.title: Registry, files and named objects
artifacts.summary: Registry keys, files, directories, pipes, devices, mutexes and window classes left by virtualisation software.

container.title: Containers and application sandboxes
container.summary: Docker/Podman/LXC/WSL/gVisor, Sandboxie, Windows Sandbox and similar isolation layers.

emulator.title: Emulators and compatibility layers
emulator.summary: Android emulators (goldfish/ranchu, Genymotion, BlueStacks...), iOS simulators, Wine, QEMU TCG.

mobile_device.title: Telephony, sensors and radios
mobile_device.summary: SIM/IMEI/operator, sensors, camera, Bluetooth and other mobile hardware a real phone has.

timing.title: Timing
timing.summary: RDTSC/CPUID VM-exit cost, clock drift between time sources, sleep acceleration, uptime.

human.title: Human interaction
human.summary: Mouse movement and clicks, keyboard input, foreground window changes, idle time.

wear_and_tear.title: Wear and tear
wear_and_tear.summary: History, recent files, installed software, logs, caches and other traces of a lived-in machine.

identity.title: Identity and locale
identity.summary: User, host and domain names, language, keyboard layout, time zone, sample file name and path.

analysis_tools.title: Analysis tools and agents
analysis_tools.summary: Debuggers, monitors, sniffers, sandbox agents and their processes, windows, files and ports.

debugger.title: Debugger detection
debugger.summary: PEB flags, debug ports and objects, hardware breakpoints, exception-based tricks, ptrace/TracerPid.

instrumentation.title: Hooks and instrumentation
instrumentation.summary: Inline/IAT hooks, injected modules, tracing frameworks, VMI and syscall-latency side channels.

network.title: Network environment
network.summary: MAC OUI, default sandbox subnets, DNS sinkholes, simulated internet, cloud metadata, proxies.

os_config.title: OS configuration
os_config.summary: Security features turned off (AV, UAC, SIP, Secure Boot), debug/test boot modes, activation, update state.

integrity.title: Device integrity (root / jailbreak)
integrity.summary: Root, jailbreak, unlocked boot loaders, debuggable builds, hooking frameworks on mobile devices.

very_common.meaning: Seen in a large share of evasive commodity malware (e.g. CPUID hypervisor bit, VM process/registry lists).

common.meaning: Regularly seen across several unrelated families.

occasional.meaning: Documented in a handful of families or loaders.

rare.meaning: Single families, targeted tooling or specialist protectors.

research.meaning: Published technique with little or no observed use in the wild.

effort_scale.1: Minutes: a guest setting, registry value or file change on the running image.
effort_scale.2: Hours: rebuild or re-snapshot the golden image (install software, rename accounts, generate history).
effort_scale.3: A day: change the VM definition or the analysis engine configuration (devices, firmware strings, plugin flags).
effort_scale.4: Days: patch and rebuild firmware, the hypervisor or the instrumentation engine.
effort_scale.5: Architectural: needs different hardware, bare metal, or accepting the residual risk.

fix_layers.guest-runtime: A setting inside the running guest that does not survive a re-snapshot unless committed.
fix_layers.guest-image: The golden image contents (software, accounts, history, configuration).
fix_layers.vm-config: The VM definition (xl.cfg / libvirt XML / emulator AVD config): devices, CPU model, memory.
fix_layers.firmware: hvmloader / SeaBIOS / OVMF / SMBIOS and ACPI tables presented to the guest.
fix_layers.hypervisor: Xen / KVM / QEMU behaviour (CPUID policy, timers, exits), usually a patch.
fix_layers.analysis-engine: The instrumentation stack (DRAKVUF plugins, injector, agents).
fix_layers.network: The analysis network (DNS, simulated internet, routing, addressing).
fix_layers.host-hardware: Physical host choice: CPU generation, bare metal, real phones.
